At IIT Madras, that question is driving a new approach to accessibility, innovation and rehabilitation. From Chennai to Colombia, Zioon87PR is showcasing the work of IIT Madras’ National Centre for Assistive Health Technologies (NCAHT-IITM) to a global audience. Established in 2023 through the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) and implemented by the TTK Centre for Rehabilitation Research and Device Development (R2D2), the Centre brings users, researchers and innovators together to explore and develop assistive solutions. Cyber fraud doesn’t discriminate by education. A new IIT Madras study reveals how even highly educated and digitally experienced professionals can fall victim to financial cybercrime. Based on interviews with 33 victims across five Indian cities, the study found that fraudsters often exploit moments of fear, stress, financial pressure and urgency to disrupt decision-making. Victims included IT professionals, bankers, doctors, finance and management professionals, public-sector officers and even individuals with cybersecurity certifications. Losses ranged from a few thousand rupees to over ₹1 crore, with victims also reporting shame, sleeplessness, depression and strained family relationships. Led by Prof. P. Kandaswamy, IPS (Retd), and Prof. Nandan Sudarsanam, IIT Madras, with Prof. Akanksha Jaiswal and Prof. Ameeta Fernando, the research highlights why cybercrime prevention must go beyond “be careful online” messaging. Where ideas meet intelligence, collaboration takes centre stage! From statistical learning to Generative AI, the inaugural ICSL-DSGA 2026 brought together researchers, academics, students and industry experts from around the world at Sunway University, Malaysia. Organised in collaboration with IIT Madras, the conference explored emerging developments across Data Science, Machine Learning, Deep Learning, NLP, Computer Vision, Healthcare Analytics, Robotics and Autonomous Systems. The numbers tell the scale of the exchange: 29 in-person and 157 online presentations, with participation from nine countries. Another milestone was the signing of an MoU between Sunway University and IIT Madras, creating new opportunities for academic and research collaboration. A story of courage, environmental justice and the power of lived experience now reaches a wider audience through The Life-Giver, translated from the Malayalam memoir Jeevadayini. The book has been translated by Professor Swarnalatha Rangarajan, Department of Humanities and Social Sciences, IIT Madras, and Dr Sreejith Varma, a former PhD scholar at IIT Madras, who currently works at VIT Vellore. The memoir narrates Leelakumariamma’s remarkable struggle against endosulfan spraying in Kerala’s Kasaragod district. After witnessing the devastating impact of chemical pesticides and losing her brother to endosulfan exposure, she embarked on a determined legal battle that ultimately contributed to a life-saving ban on the pesticide. Through this translation, the story of her courage, resilience and commitment to ecological justice reaches a wider readership, highlighting the urgent need for responsible environmental citizenship. Looking to accelerate your leadership journey while continuing to work? The Department of Management Studies (DoMS), IIT Madras, has opened applications for its two-year Executive MBA programme, designed for working professionals seeking advanced management education without stepping away from their careers. The Senate-approved IIT Madras degree programme offers weekend classes on campus, enabling professionals to balance work and learning while gaining access to the IIT Madras Alumni Community. The programme features 31 courses—17 core and 14 electives—across functional foundations, integrated perspectives, global leadership and specialised areas, with 930 teaching hours. Since 2023, the programme has also offered an International Immersion Programme, along with new industry-relevant courses. Great technologies need more than a breakthrough—they need time, capital and the right ecosystem to grow. IIT Madras is taking a step towards enabling that journey with the first close of the IIT Madras Unicorn Frontier Fund I, launched with IIT Madras Research Park and Unicorn India Ventures. With a target corpus of ₹600–1,000 crore, the fund will back IP-led, engineering-intensive deep-tech startups, particularly in areas such as robotics, space, defence and semiconductors. Alumni participation has already crossed ₹150 crore, reflecting strong support for deep-tech entrepreneurship. The fund will focus largely on early-stage ventures at TRL 3–4, offering patient capital, technical mentorship and institutional networks through their longer development and commercialisation journeys. The programme will support innovations across energy technology, energy infrastructure, carbon utilisation, circular economy and resource efficiency. What if building a career isn’t about finding the “perfect” path—but staying ready to adapt as the path evolves? In the latest episode of The Prof. Mahesh Podcast, IIT Madras hosts Mr Sanjeev Sanyal, Member, Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister, for a wide-ranging conversation on careers, uncertainty and an AI-driven future. Drawing from his own journey across economics, Oxford, financial markets, writing and public policy, Mr Sanyal highlights the value of flexibility, experimentation and persistence. He also challenges the pressure to discover a lifelong “passion” at 18 and encourages students to explore, eliminate what doesn’t work and remain open to new possibilities. The conversation also looks at how AI may reshape careers and why adaptability and lifelong learning will become increasingly important. 🎙️ Watch the full episode: https://t.co/XushjHY8k6 @iitmadras @sanjeevsanyal #IITMadras #ProfMaheshPodcast #CareerChoices #AI
